papers.title: A fatty acid amide activates myeloid cells and improves neurovascular outcomes in retinal degeneration.
papers.did: Used an unbiased high-resolution metabolomics screen to identify a dysregulated fatty acid amide and delivered it via organosilane-modified porous silicon nanoparticles in a mouse model of photoreceptor degeneration.
papers.found: Erucamide activated retinal myeloid cells, upregulating angiogenic and neurotrophic cytokines that limited vascular and neuronal degeneration; TMEM19 was identified as its binding protein required for neuroprotection.
papers.used: High-resolution metabolomics screening, nanoparticle-based in vivo delivery, mouse model of retinal degeneration.
papers.why: Reveals a previously unknown fatty acid amide pathway modulating neuroimmune interactions in retinal disease and proposes erucamide and analogs as candidate therapeutics.
papers.anchor_quote: erucamide, a 22:1 monounsaturated omega-9 fatty acid amide, is highly dysregulated during photoreceptor degeneration in mice

papers.title: Genetic and pharmacological inactivation of peptidoglycan remodeling increases antibiotic susceptibility of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium.
papers.did: Genetically and pharmacologically inactivated the peptidoglycan hydrolase SagA in vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) to test effects on antibiotic susceptibility.
papers.found: sagA deletion impaired peptidoglycan remodeling and growth and increased vancomycin activity; newly identified covalent NlpC/P60 inhibitors similarly increased vancomycin efficacy across genetically distinct VREfm clinical isolates.
papers.used: Genetic deletion (sagA knockout), covalent enzyme inhibitor discovery, ex vivo and in vivo VREfm infection models.
papers.why: Identifies peptidoglycan hydrolases as druggable targets to restore antibiotic efficacy against a major drug-resistant hospital pathogen.
papers.anchor_quote: genetic deletion of sagA impaired VREfm peptidoglycan remodeling, growth and increased the activity of vancomycin

papers.title: A Global Ligandability Map of Tryptoline Butynamide Stereoprobes Identifies Covalent Inhibitors of the Actin Maturation Protease.
papers.did: Compared covalent ligandability maps of stereochemically defined acrylamide versus butynamide stereoprobes built on a common tryptoline core using activity-based protein profiling.
papers.found: Butynamides, despite lower proteome-wide reactivity, preferentially engaged a diverse set of proteins including the actin maturation protease (ACTMAP), reacting with its catalytic nucleophile and causing accumulation of unprocessed actin.
papers.used: Activity-based protein profiling (ABPP), cysteine-reactive covalent stereoprobes, human cancer cell proteomics.
papers.why: Establishes the butynamide as a differentiated cysteine-directed electrophile that expands the ligandable human proteome for chemical probe and drug discovery.
papers.anchor_quote: the butynamides, despite exhibiting attenuated intrinsic and proteome-wide reactivity, preferentially engage a diverse set of proteins in human cancer cells

papers.title: Global genetic interaction network of a human cell maps conserved principles and informs functional interpretation of gene co-essentiality profiles.
papers.did: Built a genome-scale genetic interaction map in human haploid HAP1 cells using CRISPR-based perturbation of roughly 4 million gene pairs.
papers.found: Generated approximately 89,000 high-confidence gene-gene interactions organized into hierarchical modules corresponding to protein complexes, pathways, and cellular compartments.
papers.used: CRISPR-based combinatorial perturbation screening, HAP1 human haploid cell line, comparison against the DepMap co-essentiality network.
papers.why: Provides a data-driven map for interpreting gene function and cancer-cell-line-specific genetic dependencies useful for identifying therapeutic targets.
papers.anchor_quote: The resulting network comprises ∼89,000 high-confidence gene-gene interactions, organizing genes into hierarchical modules corresponding to protein complexes and pathways

papers.title: A recipe for chaos: Extrachromosomal DNA and the hallmarks of cancer.
papers.did: Reviews and synthesizes research on extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) in cancer and integrates it into the Hallmarks of Cancer framework.
papers.found: ecDNA causes untethering of oncogenic elements from chromosomal inheritance, generating genomic chaos and accelerated tumor evolution with therapeutic vulnerabilities distinct from mutation-targeting approaches.
papers.used: Literature synthesis and conceptual review of ecDNA biology.
papers.why: Offers a holistic framework for understanding therapy resistance in aggressive cancers and charts directions for future ecDNA-focused research.
papers.anchor_quote: oncogenic genetic elements untether from chromosomes and no longer follow Mendelian inheritance, genomic chaos and accelerated evolution ensue

papers.title: High-throughput ligand diversification to discover chemical inducers of proximity.
papers.did: Used sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange-based high-throughput chemistry to install 3,163 diverse building blocks onto ENL and BRD4 ligands and screened the resulting analogs for degrader activity.
papers.found: Identified dHTC1, an ENL degrader that recruits the CRL4-CRBN complex through an extended protein-protein interface, and dHTC3, a molecular glue that dimerizes BRD4 bromodomain 1 to SCF-FBXO3, an E3 ligase not previously accessible for chemical rewiring.
papers.used: High-throughput chemistry (HTC), sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange chemistry, chemical inducer of proximity (CIP) screening.
papers.why: Introduces a scalable tool for discovering new chemical inducers of proximity and new degrader effectors, advancing proximity pharmacology.
papers.anchor_quote: This revealed dHTC1, an ENL degrader that recruits CRL4 CRBN complex through an extended interface of protein-protein contacts and only engages CRBN after pre-forming the ENL:dHTC1 complex

papers.title: Targeting extrachromosomal DNA in human cancers.
papers.did: Reviews therapeutic and detection approaches for extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) in human cancers and proposes future directions for ecDNA-focused research.
papers.found: ecDNA drives rapid tumor evolution, metabolic adaptation, and treatment resistance, and its presence in precancerous lesions is associated with poor patient outcomes.
papers.used: Literature review synthesizing ecDNA biology and chemical proteomics approaches to therapeutic development.
papers.why: Charts a roadmap from bench to bedside for detecting and therapeutically targeting ecDNA-driven cancers.
papers.anchor_quote: ecDNA drives rapid tumour evolution, metabolic adaptation and treatment resistance

papers.title: Integrated phenotypic screening and chemical proteomics identifies ETF1 ligands that modulate viral translation and replication.
papers.did: Performed phenotypic screening of stereochemically defined photoreactive small molecules (photo-stereoprobes) and used structure-activity relationship-guided chemical proteomics to identify their cellular target.
papers.found: Photo-stereoprobes stereoselectively suppressed SARS-CoV-2 replication, targeted eukaryotic translation termination factor 1 (ETF1), modulated programmed ribosomal frameshifting without degrading ETF1, and also inhibited other viruses with similar frameshifting mechanisms.
papers.used: Phenotypic screening, photoreactive stereoprobes, chemical proteomics, recombinant protein binding assays.
papers.why: Identifies a mechanistically distinct host-targeted antiviral strategy relevant to broad-spectrum antiviral drug development.
papers.anchor_quote: the photo-stereoprobes modulate programmed ribosomal frameshifting mechanisms essential for SARS-CoV-2 infection without causing ETF1 degradation

papers.title: Cysteine Reactivity Profiling Identifies Host Regulators of Mycobacterium tuberculosis Replication in Human Macrophages.
papers.did: Applied cysteine-directed activity-based protein profiling (ABPP) to map proteome-wide cysteine reactivity changes in THP-1 monocytes and primary human macrophages during Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection.
papers.found: Quantified 148 cysteine residues with altered reactivity across both cell types, and knockdown of a subset of the proteins bearing infection-induced reactivity significantly altered Mtb replication in THP-1 monocytes.
papers.used: Cysteine-directed activity-based protein profiling, THP-1 monocytes, primary human monocyte-derived macrophages, gene knockdown.
papers.why: Defines previously unrecognized host proteins involved in antimicrobial defense, providing a resource for studying innate immune regulation during tuberculosis infection.
papers.anchor_quote: we quantified 148 cysteine residues with altered reactivity

papers.title: Ophiobolin A impacts mitochondrial redox biology in an epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-specific manner.
papers.did: Used mammary epithelial and breast cancer cell line models with and without EMT features, combined with mass spectrometry, to characterize how ophiobolin A (OpA) selectively affects EMT-positive cells.
papers.found: Identified the mitochondrial glutathione transporter SLC25A40 as an OpA-interacting protein in EMT(+) cells; OpA disrupted glycolysis, oxidative metabolism, and TCA cycle metabolite abundance, and activated NRF2-ARE antioxidant defenses.
papers.used: Mass spectrometry-based target identification, trans-mitochondrial cybrids, EMT breast cancer cell models, NRF2 activator CDDO pretreatment.
papers.why: Clarifies the mitochondrial mechanism behind OpA's selective toxicity toward EMT-positive cancer cells, informing its potential as a metastasis-targeted therapeutic.

papers.title: Structural and mechanistic analysis of covalent ligands targeting the RNA-binding protein NONO.
papers.did: Solved the crystal structure of an (R)-SKBG-1:NONO complex and tested a lower-reactivity chlorofluoroacetamide analog, (R,R)-GL-373, targeting the same binding pocket.
papers.found: The structure confirmed covalent modification of cysteine-145 near NONO's RNA-binding interface; GL-373 retained SKBG-1's pharmacological properties, including blockade of estrogen receptor expression in breast cancer cells, while showing much greater proteome-wide selectivity.
papers.used: X-ray crystallography, covalent chloroacetamide and chlorofluoroacetamide chemical probes, breast cancer cell models.
papers.why: Demonstrates that the RNA-binding protein NONO can be selectively targeted with covalent ligands to suppress pro-tumorigenic gene expression.
papers.anchor_quote: confirms covalent modification of cysteine-145 at a pocket proximal to the RNA-binding interface of the protein

papers.title: Complexoform-restricted covalent TRMT112 ligands that allosterically agonize METTL5.
papers.did: Used chemical proteomics to discover bicyclopyrrolidine acrylamide stereoprobes reacting with cysteine-100 of the adaptor protein TRMT112 and solved a cocrystal structure of the resulting complex.
papers.found: Stereoprobe reactivity with TRMT112 was negligible on the uncomplexed protein but was restored exclusively in the presence of METTL5, and stereoprobe binding allosterically agonized METTL5 through a composite pocket templated by METTL5.
papers.used: Chemical proteomics, covalent acrylamide stereoprobes, X-ray cocrystallography.
papers.why: Shows how covalent ligands can achieve complex-specific ('complexoform') pharmacology on a pleiotropic adaptor protein, enabling selective modulation of one function of a multifunctional hub.
papers.anchor_quote: the stereoprobes showed negligible reactivity with uncomplexed recombinant TRMT112 and we found that this interaction was restored exclusively in the presence of METTL5 but not other MTs

papers.title: Pharmacological targeting of the JAK-STAT pathway: new concepts and emerging indications.
papers.did: Reviews mechanistic, structural, and clinical advances in pharmacologically targeting the JAK-STAT signaling pathway.
papers.found: Fifteen JAK inhibitors are approved for immunological and hematological diseases, though safety restrictions limit their clinical use, and no STAT inhibitor has yet received clinical approval.
papers.used: Literature review of JAK and STAT inhibitor drug development and structural biology.
papers.why: Surveys emerging therapeutic indications and strategies for improving the potency, selectivity, and safety of JAK-STAT-targeted drugs.
papers.anchor_quote: Fifteen JAK inhibitors are approved for several immunological and haematological diseases, offering significant benefits for patients

papers.title: Mapping cellular targets of covalent cancer drugs in the entire mammalian body.
papers.did: Developed volumetric clearing-assisted tissue click chemistry (vCATCH) combined with HYBRiD tissue clearing and virtual reality to image covalent drug targets throughout the entire adult mouse body.
papers.found: Mapped in vivo targets of the clinical cancer drugs afatinib and ibrutinib at cellular resolution, recapitulating their known pharmacological distribution and revealing previously unreported tissue and cell-type engagement potentially linked to off-target effects.
papers.used: Click chemistry-based tissue labeling (vCATCH), whole-body tissue clearing (HYBRiD), virtual reality visualization, clinical cancer drugs afatinib and ibrutinib.
papers.why: Provides a body-wide, unbiased platform for mapping covalent drug engagement at cellular resolution, useful for understanding off-target drug effects.
papers.anchor_quote: vCATCH offers cellular-resolution drug imaging in the entire adult mouse

papers.title: A chemical-genetic interaction between PAF1 and ENL/AF9 YEATS inhibition.
papers.did: Performed a CRISPR/Cas9-based genetic modifier screen in models of intrinsic and acquired resistance to ENL/AF9 YEATS domain inhibitors and constructed isogenic leukemia models using identified PAF1 resistance alleles.
papers.found: Identified in-frame deletions of PAF1 that confer resistance to ENL/AF9 YEATS domain inhibitors, yet downregulation of ENL target genes remained shared between sensitive and resistant leukemia cells.
papers.used: CRISPR/Cas9 genetic modifier screening, isogenic leukemia cell models, small-molecule YEATS domain inhibitors.
papers.why: Shows that suppression of ENL target genes alone is not sufficient to explain the anti-leukemia effects of ENL/AF9 antagonists, refining understanding of drug resistance mechanisms.
papers.anchor_quote: identified in-frame deletions of the essential transcriptional regulator, PAF1, that confer resistance to ENL/AF9 YEATS domain inhibitors

papers.title: Development of a novel 18F-labeled reversible-binding radioligand for imaging monoacylglycerol lipase with positron emission tomography.
papers.did: Developed and pharmacologically evaluated a new series of reversible MAGL inhibitor candidates based on a piperazinyl azetidine diamide scaffold, then radiolabeled the lead compound with fluorine-18 for PET imaging.
papers.found: Compound 3 showed the best pharmacological performance and, as [18F]3 ([18F]MAGL-2011), exhibited favorable brain uptake, excellent in vivo binding specificity, and dose-dependent PET signal reduction upon target occupancy by a therapeutic MAGL inhibitor.
papers.used: Radioligand synthesis (fluorine-18 labeling), autoradiography, PET imaging, ex vivo biodistribution and metabolite analysis in rodents.
papers.why: Provides a promising MAGL-specific PET ligand to facilitate clinical drug development and quantify target occupancy in patients with neurodegenerative disorders.
papers.anchor_quote: [ 18 F] 3 ([ 18 F]MAGL-2011) has the potential to serve as an effective MAGL PET ligand

papers.title: Mitochondrial ABHD11 inhibition drives sterol metabolism to modulate T-cell effector function.
papers.did: Pharmacologically inhibited the mitochondrial hydrolase ABHD11 in human and mouse T-cells and tested effects in murine models of accelerated type 1 diabetes.
papers.found: ABHD11 inhibition dampened cytokine production in T-cells via increased 24,25-epoxycholesterol biosynthesis and LXR activation, and delayed diabetes onset in female mice while suppressing cytokine production in antigen-specific T-cells.
papers.used: Pharmacological hydrolase inhibitors, human and mouse T-cell assays, murine type 1 diabetes models, patient autoimmunity cohorts.
papers.why: Identifies ABHD11 as a promising drug target for T-cell-mediated inflammatory and autoimmune diseases such as type 1 diabetes and rheumatoid arthritis.
papers.anchor_quote: targeting ABHD11 suppresses cytokine production in antigen-specific T-cells and delays the onset of diabetes in vivo in female mice

papers.title: NONO Maintains SREBP-Regulated Cholesterol Biosynthesis via RNA Binding in Neuroblastoma.
papers.did: Knocked down NONO in high-risk neuroblastoma patient-derived and KELLY cell lines and tested the covalent RNA-binding modulator (R)-SKBG-1 for effects on cholesterol regulation.
papers.found: NONO knockdown reduced cholesterol levels and SREBP family mRNA/protein expression; only wild-type (not RNA-binding-deficient mutant) NONO could restore SREBP levels, and (R)-SKBG-1 significantly decreased cholesterol and SREBP target gene expression.
papers.used: RNA-seq, gene knockdown, RNA recognition motif mutant rescue experiments, small-molecule RNA-binding modulator (R)-SKBG-1.
papers.why: Suggests targeting NONO's RNA-binding activity as a potential therapeutic strategy against aggressive, cholesterol-dependent neuroblastoma.
papers.anchor_quote: (R)-SKBG-1, a small molecule that modulates the RNA binding activity of NONO, hence altering its subnuclear distribution, significantly decreased cholesterol levels and SREBP target gene expression in KELLY cells
